### The "16 slots" reading was wrong, twice over

Two retractions belong here, because the wrong version was committed before
the inventory was checked properly.

Reading slots 0..19 produced a report where the same addresses appeared under
different labels with identical values - `0x02cf106c` was `"SWAPTEST.cube"`
both as "FILE_ID slot 0" and as "IS_EXIST slot 16". The conclusion drawn from
that, that each family is 16 wide and the model has only 16 slots, was wrong.

The real cause was a throwaway extraction script of mine that took the
inventory's slot 0 and slot 1 ids, computed a step of 1, and assumed
`base + n` from there. The inventory itself is right and has **no** colliding
ids: `IS_EXIST_USER_LUT15` is `0x02cf106b` and `IS_EXIST_USER_LUT16` jumps to
`0x02cf141e`. All 250 names resolve to 250 distinct addresses. The reader now
carries the real run table and `address()` looks the slot up in it.

The earlier "slots 16..49 return nothing, so they are not provisioned" reading
was wrong too - nothing ever came back empty. Both wrong readings came from
reading real properties under the wrong names.

The real cause was a throwaway extraction script of mine that took the
inventory's slot 0 and slot 1 ids, computed a step of 1, and assumed
`base + n` from there. The inventory itself is right and has **no** colliding
ids: `IS_EXIST_USER_LUT15` is `0x02cf106b` and `IS_EXIST_USER_LUT16` jumps to
`0x02cf141e`. All 250 names resolve to 250 distinct addresses. The reader now
carries the real run table and `address()` looks the slot up in it.

The earlier "slots 16..49 return nothing, so they are not provisioned" reading
was wrong too - nothing ever came back empty. Both wrong readings came from
reading real properties under the wrong names.

carries the real run table and `address()` looks the slot up in it.

carries the real run table and `address()` looks the slot up in it.

both as "FILE_ID slot 0" and as "IS_EXIST slot 16". The conclusion drawn from
that, that each family is 16 wide and the model has only 16 slots, was wrong.

The real cause was a throwaway extraction script of mine that took the
inventory's slot 0 and slot 1 ids, computed a step of 1, and assumed
`base + n` from there. The inventory itself is right and has **no** colliding
ids: `IS_EXIST_USER_LUT15` is `0x02cf106b` and `IS_EXIST_USER_LUT16` jumps to
`0x02cf141e`. All 250 names resolve to 250 distinct addresses. The reader now
carries the real run table and `address()` looks the slot up in it.

The earlier "slots 16..49 return nothing, so they are not provisioned" reading
was wrong too - nothing ever came back empty. Both wrong readings came from
reading real properties under the wrong names.
